prompt:
Feature: structured recipe times, stored as seconds next to the free text.

Recipe total, prep and cook times are only free text today. Imports turn a schema.org duration such as "PT1H30M" into English words ("1 hour 30 minutes", or "none" for a zero time) whatever the user's language, migrations from other apps write their own English, and the schema.org JSON Mealie serves for a recipe page repeats that text where schema.org expects ISO 8601 durations. Users want real durations that can be localized and relied on, while keeping free text for what is not a duration ("overnight", "about an hour").

Expected:

1. Recipe schema and API
- RecipeSummary (so also Recipe and every response that embeds it) gets total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds (JSON totalTimeSeconds, prepTimeSeconds, performTimeSeconds): optional whole seconds, default null, from 0 to 2147483647 (the Postgres INTEGER max). None, 0, 5400 and 2147483647 are kept as given; -1 and 2147483648 fail validation (building a RecipeSummary raises pydantic's ValidationError, which is a ValueError).
- The text fields total_time, prep_time, cook_time and perform_time stay, with their current coercion (None stays None, "" stays "", 10 gives "10", 2.25 gives "2.25"). There is no structured cook_time: perform_time_seconds is the structured cook time. Wherever this feature turns a time into seconds, that time's text becomes null; text is kept only for what is not a duration.
- The API stores and returns the seconds and text a client sends. Saving a recipe never reinterprets its text (a PUT with "totalTime": "PT25M" keeps that text), and a zip export and re-import keeps all four text fields.

2. Database and Alembic migration
- The recipes table gets three nullable INTEGER columns, total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds, mapped on RecipeModel, so recipes persist and return the new fields.
- A new Alembic migration adds them: revision id 27621d27c7e1, down revision 3527efeeec34 (the current head), message "add structured recipe times", create date 2026-09-24 13:16:56. Name its file with the project's migration file template (file_template in alembic.ini), so the name contains the revision id and sorts after every existing migration (tests/unit_tests/test_alembic.py checks that the sorted files chain). Tests find it with ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*27621d27c7e1*.py"), load it standalone with import_file from tests/utils/alembic_reader.py, and call its functions while the test module is imported.
- Upgrade adds the columns, then converts the existing text in total_time, prep_time and perform_time (cook_time is left alone): when parse_seconds (below) reads a text, its seconds are stored and the text is set to NULL; otherwise, when is_empty_time is true for it (the "none" the scraper used to write for a zero time), the text is set to NULL; anything else stays exactly as it was. Downgrade first writes format_seconds(seconds) into each of those text fields that is NULL while its seconds are set, then drops the three columns.
- The migration module itself defines these functions, which tests call directly. The parsing lives in the migration and does not use the scraper code, so later scraper changes cannot change what the migration did.
  - load_unit_words(locales_dir=<the backend translations folder, mealie/lang/messages>) returns a dict from unit word to unit name. It reads every *.json file in the folder and, from its "datetime" object, the entries "day", "hour", "minute" and "second" (each like "hour|hours"). Each entry is split on "|", every word is stripped and casefolded, and empty words are skipped. Files that cannot be read, are not valid JSON or are not a JSON object are skipped. A word listed under two different units (in one file or across files) is ambiguous and must not appear in the result at all. Example: aa-AA.json {"datetime": {"hour": "tick|ticks", "minute": "min"}}, bb-BB.json {"datetime": {"second": "tick|tock"}} and broken.json containing "{" give exactly {"ticks": "hour", "min": "minute", "tock": "second"}.
  - build_component_pattern(unit_words) builds, from those words, the matcher for one "<number><unit word>" component (a compiled regular expression). Tests build it once and only pass it to parse_seconds.
  - parse_seconds(value, unit_words, pattern) returns the duration in whole seconds, or None unless the entire value reads as one clear duration:
    a. None, "" and whitespace only give None; surrounding whitespace is ignored.
    b. A bare number (digits, optionally a dot and more digits; no sign, no comma) is minutes: "30" gives 1800, "1.5" gives 90.
    c. A value starting with "P" or "p" is read only as an ISO 8601 duration, case-insensitively: "PT15M" 900, "PT1H30M" 5400, "pt1h" 3600, "P1DT2H" 93600, "PT90S" 90. Years and months have no fixed length, so "P1M" and "P1Y" give None, and "PTXM" (invalid) gives None.
    d. Anything else must consist entirely of one or more components, each a number as in (b) followed by a unit word from unit_words, matched case-insensitively. The space between number and word, and between components, is optional, but a word must be followed by whitespace, a digit or the end of the text. Units must come largest first (day, hour, minute, second), each at most once. Read: "1 hour 30 minutes" 5400, "1 Hour" 3600, "2 days 4 hours" 187200, "45 seconds" 45, "1 Stunde 30 Minuten" 5400, "2 heures 15 minutes" 8100, "1 時間 30 分" 5400, "1時間30分" 5400, "1.5 hours" 5400, "  20 minutes  " 1200. None for "about 30 minutes", "30 minutes, plus overnight", "1 hour and 30 minutes", "1 hour, 30 minutes", "Overnight", "none", "30 minutes 1 hour" (out of order), "10 minutes 5 minutes" (repeated), and "30 mins" and "1 hr" (not words from the translations).
    e. In every case the total must be a whole number of seconds (nothing is rounded), above 0 and at most 2147483647, otherwise None: "0", "PT0M" and "0 minutes" (zero), "PT0.5S" and "0.001" (not whole seconds), "P30000D" (too large).
  - is_empty_time(value) returns a real bool: True when the value, stripped and casefolded, is exactly "none" ("none", " None "), and False for None, "", "none needed" and "30 minutes".
  - format_seconds(seconds) returns English text in the scraper's old shape: days, hours, minutes and seconds, zero parts left out, singular for 1, separated by single spaces. 60 gives "1 minute", 5400 "1 hour 30 minutes", 93690 "1 day 2 hours 1 minute 30 seconds".

3. Cleaning (the scraper's cleaner module, the one with clean, clean_time and pretty_print_timedelta; tests call these as cleaner.<name>)
- A new function clean_duration(time_entry) returns whole seconds when the entry is a structured duration, and None for anything that should stay text:
  - True or False gives None (a bool is not a number of minutes).
  - An int or float is minutes: 30 gives 1800, 1.5 gives 90.
  - A string, stripped: a bare number (digits, optionally a dot and more digits) is minutes ("30" gives 1800); otherwise it is read as an ISO 8601 duration, case-insensitively: "PT1H30M" 5400, "pt15m" 900, "P1DT1H" 90000, "P1W" 604800, "PT1M1.53S" 62. Anything else gives None: "", "1 hour 30 minutes", "P1M" and "P1Y" (no fixed length), "PT-3H" (invalid).
  - A timedelta gives its length (timedelta(hours=1) gives 3600). A dict with "minValue" gives that value's result ({"minValue": "PT1H"} gives 3600). A non-empty list gives its first item's result (["PT1H", "PT2H"] gives 3600). None and anything else give None.
  - The result is rounded to the nearest second and must be above 0 and at most 2147483647, else None: 0, "PT0M", "PT" (a duration with no parts counts as zero), -5, "P30000D" and float("inf") all give None.
- clean_time(time_entry, translator) keeps writing durations as words with pretty_print_timedelta, with these rules (en-US translator):
  - None, "" and " " give None. Text that is not a duration is kept: "invalid" gives "invalid".
  - timedelta(minutes=30) gives "30 minutes"; "PT2H30M" "2 hours 30 minutes"; "PT30M" "30 minutes"; "PT2H" "2 hours"; "P1DT1H1M1S" and "P1DT1H1M1.53S" both "1 day 1 hour 1 minute 1 second" (fractions of a second are dropped); "P1D" "1 day"; "P3D" "3 days"; "P1W" "7 days".
  - Durations of zero or less give None, never "none": "PT", "PT0S", timedelta(0) and -5 (minutes).
  - ISO-looking text that is not a usable duration is kept exactly as given: "P1M" (months), "-PT1H" (negative) and "PT-3H".
- cleaner.clean(recipe_data, translator), for a dict or a Recipe, handles totalTime, prepTime and performTime this way: when the matching totalTimeSeconds, prepTimeSeconds or performTimeSeconds is missing or null and clean_duration reads the time, those seconds are stored and the text becomes null; otherwise the text is cleaned with clean_time as today. Seconds that are already set are kept as they are, and the text is still cleaned. {"name": "Test Recipe", "totalTime": "PT1H30M", "prepTime": 20, "performTime": "about an hour"} gives total_time_seconds 5400 and total_time None, prep_time_seconds 1200 and prep_time None, perform_time_seconds None and perform_time "about an hour". {"name": "Test Recipe", "totalTime": "PT2H", "totalTimeSeconds": 60} gives total_time_seconds 60 and total_time "2 hours".
- pretty_print_timedelta and the cleaner's other helpers (clean_string, clean_image, clean_instructions, clean_ingredients, clean_yield, clean_categories, clean_tags, clean_nutrition, clean_notes) keep their current behaviour, and clean still accepts the recipe JSON files in tests/data/json.

4. Scraping a URL: a recipe scraped from schema.org data (RecipeScraperPackage.clean_scraper followed by cleaner.clean, as the URL import does) gets structured times too, the perform time coming from performTime, else cookTime. ld+json with totalTime "PT1H30M", prepTime "PT20M" and cookTime "PT1H10M" ends with seconds 5400, 1200 and 4200 for total, prep and perform, and all three texts null. Times that are not durations stay text, and clean_scraper still keeps the schema.org notes.

5. Migrations from other apps (POST /api/groups/migrations) store structured times instead of English text. For the recipes below, the result is given as (total, prep, perform) seconds, and all three time texts are null:
- Nextcloud: totalTime, prepTime and cookTime in recipe.json are ISO durations for total, prep and perform. "Skillet Shepherd's Pie" (totalTime PT1H25M, prepTime PT0H15M, cookTime PT1H10M) gives (5100, 900, 4200).
- Tandoor: working_time and waiting_time are minutes; perform is working_time, total is working_time + waiting_time, there is no prep, and a zero time is null. "“Texas Red” Chili" (working_time 0, waiting_time 2) gives (120, None, None).
- My Recipe Box CSV: preparationTime, cookingTime and totalTime are minutes for prep, perform and total. "Beef & Cheese Piroshki" (preparationTime 90, cookingTime 25, totalTime 115) gives (6900, 5400, 1500); empty cells give nothing.
- Recipe Keeper: prepTime and cookTime are ISO durations for prep and perform; there is no total. "Zucchini Bread" (prepTime PT30M, cookTime PT1H) gives (None, 1800, 3600); "PT0S" gives nothing.
- Cook'n: PREPTIME and COOKTIME are minutes, for prep and perform, and total is their sum. "Fresh Fruit Pizza" (0 and 0) gives (None, None, None).
The rest of every migration is unchanged: each test archive (Paprika, Chowdown, Copy Me That, Mealie alpha and Plan to Eat too) still imports every entry successfully, with its timeline event, nutrition, categories, yield and notes; an upload Plan to Eat cannot read and an empty Mealie alpha recipe file are still reported as failures with the same messages.

6. AI import (POST /api/recipes/create/ai)
- The time fields of the AI recipe schema (OpenAIRecipe) ask the provider for an ISO 8601 duration (such as PT1H30M, PT30M or PT1H), or plain text when the time is not a clear duration (such as overnight). The built recipe is cleaned as in 3, so total_time "PT1H30M" is stored as totalTimeSeconds 5400 with totalTime null, and "overnight" stays text.
- With translateLanguage, the translation request carries only text: structured times are not sent ("PT1H30M" appears nowhere in that message), and the translated recipe keeps the built recipe's seconds, even though the provider's answer carries no time. Example: the build returns total_time "PT1H30M" and prep_time "overnight", the translation returns total_time null and prep_time "la nuit": exactly two recipe requests are made, the response is 201, and the stored recipe has totalTimeSeconds 5400, totalTime null, prepTimeSeconds null and prepTime "la nuit".
- Everything else in the AI import stays as it is (compiling sources, organizers, images, the translation as its own request carrying the whole recipe's text, skipping or surviving a translation, error messages and status codes, the streaming endpoint).

7. Recipe page metadata (schema.org)
- A new module-level function iso_duration(seconds) in the SPA module that serves recipe pages with metadata (the one with content_with_meta, inject_recipe_json and serve_recipe_with_meta). None or 0 give None; otherwise "PT" followed by hours with "H", minutes with "M" and seconds with "S", zero parts left out and no days: 45 gives "PT45S", 900 "PT15M", 5400 "PT1H30M", 3690 "PT1H1M30S", 93600 "PT26H".
- content_with_meta fills schema.org totalTime, prepTime and cookTime with iso_duration of total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds. Free text never goes there; without seconds the value is null. Example: total_time_seconds 5400, perform_time_seconds 3600, prep_time "a while" and cook_time "PT10M" give totalTime "PT1H30M", cookTime "PT1H" and prepTime null.
- Everything else is unchanged: the other schema.org fields and the meta tags, HTML escaping of recipe text, serving public and shared recipes, and the 404 for an unknown group or recipe, or for a private recipe or private group seen without a user.

8. Frontend
- A new composable module use-recipe-time in the recipes composables folder (the spec imports it as ../use-recipe-time from its __tests__ folder) exports three pure functions that take the locale as an argument and need no i18n setup. Unit names come from the platform's Intl unit formatting for that locale, not from the app's translation files.
  - formatDuration(seconds, locale): days, hours, minutes and seconds with the locale's long unit names, zero parts left out. In en-US: 60 gives "1 minute", 1800 "30 minutes", 3600 "1 hour", 5400 "1 hour 30 minutes", 90 "1 minute 30 seconds", 93600 "1 day 2 hours". In de-DE, 5400 starts with "1 Stunde" and ends with "30 Minuten" (how the parts are joined may vary).
  - durationUnitLabel(unit, locale), for unit "hour" or "minute": the locale's short unit name, "hr" and "min" in en-US.
  - recipeTimeDisplay(seconds, text, locale): the formatted duration (when seconds is set and not 0) followed by the trimmed text, joined by one space, empty parts left out. (10800, "plus overnight") gives "3 hours plus overnight"; (5400, null) and (5400, " ") give "1 hour 30 minutes"; (null, "overnight"), (undefined, "overnight") and (0, "overnight") give "overnight"; (null, null) and (null, "") give "".
- The recipe page, print view and recipe editor should show and edit the structured times next to the text, and the frontend API types get the three fields; that wiring is not graded.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests tests/integration_tests/test_spa.py tests/integration_tests/recipe_migration_tests tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

Frontend: `cd frontend && pnpm test:ci app/composables/recipes/__tests__/use-recipe-time.test.ts`.
